blocks.raw: # Add Dynamic Content Using Liquid
This guide provides an overview of the Liquid template language, focusing on features relevant for personalizing messages in Engage+.
blocks.text: This guide provides an overview of the Liquid template language, focusing on features relevant for personalizing messages in Engage+.

blocks.raw: # Introduction to Liquid

Liquid is a templating language used to add dynamic content. It lets you personalize your messages based on user data, making your communications more relevant and engaging. For instance, you can use liquid language to define the date format according to the customer's locale, send product recommendations based on the customer's interest, etc.
blocks.text: Liquid is a templating language used to add dynamic content. It lets you personalize your messages based on user data, making your communications more relevant and engaging. For instance, you can use liquid language to define the date format according to the customer's locale, send product recommendations based on the customer's interest, etc.

blocks.raw: Liquid expressions are supported across **SMS**, **Push notification**, **In app**, and **Email** channels and is available for all the organizations by default.
blocks.text: Liquid expressions are supported across SMS, Push notification, In app, and Email channels and is available for all the organizations by default.

blocks.raw:
> 📘 Note
>
> While creating a template in the **Creatives** section for **SMS**, **Push Notification**, **In-App**, and **Email** channels, Liquid expressions are not strictly validated at the time of creation. You can add any Liquid expressions, save the template without errors, and use **Test & Preview** within Creatives. However, ensure that all curly braces are properly closed; improperly closed `{{` or `{%` tags will still throw a validation error when saving the template.
>
> During campaign creation or journey, if the selected template contains invalid or unsupported Liquid expressions, the system will throw an error and will not allow you to select or use that template.

blocks.raw: # Basic Syntax
Liquid uses two types of markup:
blocks.text: Liquid uses two types of markup:

blocks.raw:
| Syntax Type     | Markup  | Description                      |
| :-------------- | :------ | :------------------------------- |
| Output          | `{{ }}` | Used to output dynamic content.  |
| Logic & Control | `{% %}` | Used for logic and control flow. |

rows: Used for logic and control flow.

blocks.raw:
> 🚧 Important
>
> * Make sure that all tags contain data. Inconsistency in the tags will result in a validation error.
> * When using Liquid loops `({% for %}...{% endfor %})`, ensure that all HTML referencing loop variables stay inside the loop block. Some editors may automatically reformat HTML and move elements outside the loop, which can break variables like `item` or `item.index`. Always review the code after editing to confirm the loop structure is intact.
> * When using special characters in text, such as a forward slash (`/`), use single quotes (`'`) instead of double quotes (`"`) to prevent errors. For example, `{% if generic_event_field__hotel_name == 'The Lakeside Resort/Spa' %}`

blocks.raw: # Variables
Variables allow you to insert dynamic content into your templates. Common variables might include:
blocks.text: Variables allow you to insert dynamic content into your templates. Common variables might include:

blocks.raw:
* `{{first_name}}`: The customer's first name
* `{{customer_email}}`: The customer's email address
* `{{customer_mobile}}`: The customer's mobile number
